questions.text: Two balls A and B are placed at the top of 180 m tall tower. Ball A is released from the top at $\mathrm{t}=0$ s. Ball B is thrown vertically down with an initial velocity 'u' at $\mathrm{t}=2 \mathrm{~s}$. After a certain time, both balls meet 100 m above the ground. Find the value of 'u' in $\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$. [use $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$ ] :

options.D:
30

Official Ans. by NTA (D)
Ans. (D)
Sol. Let they meet at time t.
$$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{t}=\sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{~h}}{\mathrm{~g}}}=\sqrt{\frac{2 \times 80}{10}} \\
=4 \mathrm{sec}
\end{array}$$

Time taken by ball B to meet $\mathrm{A}=2 \mathrm{sec}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\text { using } S=u t+\frac{1}{2} a t^{2} \\
-80=-u \times 2+\frac{1}{2}(-10)(2)^{2} \\
u=30
\end{array}$$

questions.text: A body of mass M at rest explodes into three pieces, in the ratio of masses 1 : 1 : 2. Two smaller pieces fly off perpendicular to each other with velocities of $30 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ and $40 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ respectively. The velocity of the third piece will be :

options.D:
$50 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)
Sol. Mass of pieces by $\frac{\mathrm{M}}{4}, \frac{\mathrm{M}}{4}, \frac{\mathrm{M}}{2}$
conserving momentum
$$\begin{array}{l}
\overrightarrow{\mathrm{P}}_{1}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{P}}_{2}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{P}}_{3}=0 \\
\overline{\mathrm{P}}_{3}=-\left(\overline{\mathrm{P}}_{1}+\overline{\mathrm{P}}_{2}\right)
\end{array}$$

As $\overline{\mathrm{P}}_{1}$ \& $\overline{\mathrm{P}}_{2}$ are perpendicular
$$\begin{array}{l}
\text { so } \mathrm{P}_{3}=\sqrt{\mathrm{P}_{1}^{2}+\mathrm{P}_{2}^{2}} \\
\mathrm{P}_{3}=(50) \frac{\mathrm{M}}{4} \\
\& \mathrm{P}_{3}=\frac{\mathrm{M}}{2} \mathrm{v} \\
\text { so } \mathrm{v}=25
\end{array}$$

steps:
Mass of pieces by $\frac{\mathrm{M}}{4}, \frac{\mathrm{M}}{4}, \frac{\mathrm{M}}{2}$
conserving momentum
$$\begin{array}{l}
\overrightarrow{\mathrm{P}}_{1}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{P}}_{2}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{P}}_{3}=0 \\
\overline{\mathrm{P}}_{3}=-\left(\overline{\mathrm{P}}_{1}+\overline{\mathrm{P}}_{2}\right)
\end{array}$$

As $\overline{\mathrm{P}}_{1}$ \& $\overline{\mathrm{P}}_{2}$ are perpendicular
$$\begin{array}{l}
\text { so } \mathrm{P}_{3}=\sqrt{\mathrm{P}_{1}^{2}+\mathrm{P}_{2}^{2}} \\
\mathrm{P}_{3}=(50) \frac{\mathrm{M}}{4} \\
\& \mathrm{P}_{3}=\frac{\mathrm{M}}{2} \mathrm{v} \\
\text { so } \mathrm{v}=25
\end{array}$$

questions.text: A spherical shell of 1 kg mass and radius R is rolling with angular speed $\omega$ on horizontal plane (as shown in figure). The magnitude of angular momentum of the shell about the origin O is $\frac{\mathrm{a}}{3} \mathrm{R}^{2} \omega$. The value of a will be :

options.D:
4

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (C)
Sol. $\mathrm{L}_{0}$ = angular momentum of shell about O.
As shell is rolling
$$\begin{array}{l}
\text { so } V_{\mathrm{cm}}=\omega R \\
L_{0}=m V_{\mathrm{cm}} R+I \omega \\
=1 \times \omega R \times R+\frac{2}{3} R^{2} \omega \\
=\frac{5}{3} R^{2} \omega \\
\text { so } a=5
\end{array}$$

questions.text:
A cylinder of fixed capacity of 44.8 litres contains helium gas at standard temperature and pressure. The amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of gas in the cylinder by $20.0^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ will be :
(Given gas constant $\mathrm{R}=8.3 \mathrm{JK}^{-1}-\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ )

options.D:
830 J

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (C)
Sol. No of moles $=\frac{44.8}{22.4}=2$
Gas is mono atomic so $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{v}}=\frac{3}{2} \mathrm{R}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\Delta Q=\mathrm{nC}_{\mathrm{v}} \Delta \mathrm{~T} \\
=2 \times \frac{3}{2} \mathrm{R}(20) \\
=60 \mathrm{R} \\
=60 \times 8.3 \\
=498 \mathrm{~J}
\end{array}$$

questions.text: A wire of length L is hanging from a fixed support. The length changes to $\mathrm{L}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{L}_{2}$ when masses 1 kg and 2 kg are suspended respectively from its free end. Then the value of L is equal to :

options.D:
$3 \mathrm{~L}_{1}-2 \mathrm{~L}_{2}$

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (C)
Sol. By Hooke's Law
so $\mathrm{F} \alpha \Delta \mathrm{L}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\frac{\mathrm{F}_{1}}{\mathrm{~F}_{2}}=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{L}_{1}}{\Delta \mathrm{~L}_{2}} \\
\frac{10}{20}=\frac{\left(\mathrm{L}_{1}-\mathrm{L}\right)}{\left(\mathrm{L}_{2}-\mathrm{L}\right)} \\
\mathrm{L}=2 \mathrm{~L}_{1}-\mathrm{L}_{2}
\end{array}$$

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R. Assertion A : The photoelectric effect does not take place, if the energy of the incident radiation is less than the work function of a metal.
Reason R : Kinetic energy of the photoelectrons is zero, if the energy of the incident radiation is equal to the work function of a metal.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.

options.A: Both $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{R}$ are correct and $\mathbf{R}$ is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: $\mathbf{A}$ is correct but $\mathbf{R}$ is not correct
options.D:
$\mathbf{A}$ is not correct but $\mathbf{R}$ is correct

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)
Sol. To free the electron from metal surface minimum energy required, is equal to the work function of that metal.
So Assertion A, is correct.
$\mathrm{hv}=\mathrm{w}_{0}+\mathrm{K} . \mathrm{E} ._{\text {max }}$
if $\mathrm{hv}=\mathrm{w}_{0}$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{K} . \mathrm{E}_{._{\text {max }}}=0$
Hence reason R, is correct, But R is not the correct explanation of A.

questions.text: A particle of mass 500 gm is moving in a straight line with velocity $v=\mathrm{bx}^{5 / 2}$. The work done by the net force during its displacement from $\mathrm{x}=0$ to $\mathrm{x}=4 \mathrm{~m}$ is : (Take $\mathrm{b}=0.25 \mathrm{~m}^{-3 / 2} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$ ).

options.D:
16 J

Official Ans. by NTA (D)
Ans. (D)
Sol. By work energy theorem
work done by net force $=\Delta \mathrm{K} . \mathrm{E}$.
$$\begin{array}{l}
\Rightarrow \mathrm{w}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}_{\mathrm{f}}^{2}-\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}_{\mathrm{i}}^{2} \\
\mathrm{w}=\frac{1}{2} \times 0.5 \times(0.25)^{2} \times(4)^{5} \\
\mathrm{w}=16 \mathrm{~J}
\end{array}$$

questions.text:
For a series LCR circuit, I vs $\omega$ curve is shown :
(a) To the left of $\omega_{\mathrm{r}}$, the circuit is mainly capacitive.
(b) To the left of $\omega_{\mathrm{r}}$, the circuit is mainly inductive.
(c) At $\omega_{\mathrm{r}}$, impedance of the circuit is equal to the resistance of the circuit.
(d) At $\omega_{\mathrm{r}}$, impedance of the circuit is 0.
$\omega$
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

options.D:
(b) and (c) only

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (C)

Sol. at $\omega_{\mathrm{r}}, \mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}}=\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}$
$$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{\omega_{\mathrm{r}} \mathrm{C}}=\omega_{\mathrm{r}} \mathrm{~L}$$

So if $\omega<\omega_{\mathrm{r}}$ then $\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{C}}$ will increase and $\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}$ will decrease.
Hence to left of $\omega_{\mathrm{r}}$ circuit is capacitive
$$\mathrm{Z}=\sqrt{\mathrm{R}^{2}+\left(\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}}-\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}\right)^{2}}$$
at $\omega_{\mathrm{r}}, \mathrm{Z}=\sqrt{\mathrm{R}^{2}+\mathrm{O}^{2}}=\mathrm{R}(\mathrm{C})$

questions.text: Two vectors $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{A}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}}$ have equal magnitudes. If magnitude of $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{A}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}}$ is equal to two times the magnitude of $\vec{A}-\vec{B}$, then the angle between $\vec{A}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}}$ will be :

options.D:
$\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)$

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (C)
Sol. $\left(\mathrm{a}^{2}+\mathrm{b}^{2}+2 \mathrm{ab} \cos \theta\right)=4\left(\mathrm{a}^{2}+\mathrm{b}^{2}-2 \mathrm{ab} \cos \theta\right)$ put $\mathrm{a}=\mathrm{b}$ we get
$$\begin{array}{l}
2 a^{2}+2 a^{2} \cos \theta=8 a^{2}-8 a^{2} \cos \theta \\
\cos \theta=\frac{3}{5}
\end{array}$$

questions.text: Using Young's double slit experiment, a monochromatic light of wavelength $5000 \AA$ produces fringes of fringe width 0.5 mm. If another monochromatic light of wavelength $6000 \AA$ is used and the separation between the slits is doubled, then the new fringe width will be :

options.D:
0.3 mm

Official Ans. by NTA (D)
Ans. (D)
Sol. Fringe width $\beta=\frac{\mathrm{D} \lambda}{\mathrm{d}}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\lambda_{1}=5000 \AA \\
\beta_{1}=\frac{D}{d}\left(5000 \times 10^{-10}\right)=5 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~m} \\
\beta_{2}=\frac{D}{(2 d)}\left(6000 \times 10^{-10}\right)=x \text { (let) }
\end{array}$$

Divide (II) \& (I)
$$\begin{array}{l}
\frac{\beta_{2}}{\beta_{1}}=\frac{3000 \times 10^{-10}}{5000 \times 10^{-10}}=\frac{x}{5 \times 10^{-4}} \\
x=3 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~m} \text { or } 0.3 \mathrm{~mm}
\end{array}$$

questions.text: Only 2\% of the optical source frequency is the available channel bandwidth for an optical communicating system operating at 1000 nm. If an audio signal requires a bandwidth of 8 kHz, how many channels can be accommodated for transmission :

options.D:
$75 \times 10^{9}$

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)
Sol. Frequency at $1000 \mathrm{~nm}=\frac{3 \times 10}{1000 \times 10^{-9}} \Rightarrow 3 \times 10^{14} \mathrm{~Hz}$ available for channel band width
$$=\frac{2}{100} \times 3 \times 10^{14} \Rightarrow 6 \times 10^{12} \mathrm{~Hz}$$

Bandwidth for 1 channel = 8000 Hz
∴ No. of channel
$$=\frac{6 \times 10^{12}}{8 \times 10^{3}} \Rightarrow \frac{600}{8} \times 10^{7}=75 \times 10^{7}$$

SECTION-B
